themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 39 this week—a 721% increase from the 4.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 15.41)—signaling a sudden deterioration in road surfaces, potholes, or street maintenance across Central Harlem that demands immediate investigation into what triggered this sharp, localized emergency.
evidence: 39 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average (8-week baseline)
No prior weeks in last 90 days approached this volume, indicating acute new problem
reporting_angles: Ground truth: Visit neighborhoods with highest complaint density; photograph worst street conditions and interview residents
Department of Transportation source: Did a specific street project fail, or has winter weather/recent work caused widespread damage?

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 32 last week—a 105% spike from the 15.6-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 3.78)—suggesting a possible sudden outbreak or systemic failure in pest management that warrants investigation into underlying causes (sanitation, construction, or weather).
evidence: 32 rodent complaints last week vs. 15.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Litter basket complaints also spiked 700% (3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 avg), suggesting garbage management breakdown enabling infestation
reporting_angles: Resident testimony: Interview households and small businesses reporting rodent sightings; map complaint hotspots
NYC Health Department / Sanitation source: Is this a seasonal uptick or sign of systemic failures in waste collection or building conditions?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints reached 18 two weeks ago—a 269% increase from the 4.9-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.54)—pointing to a possible pattern of illegal street racing, delivery congestion, or construction activity that warrants street-level reporting.
evidence: 18 vehicle noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.9 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Concurrent spike in street light condition complaints (14, 2 weeks ago) may indicate ongoing street work or traffic pattern changes
reporting_angles: Observation reporting: Spend evening/night hours on high-complaint blocks to document noise sources (vehicles, construction, deliveries)
NYPD source: Are there enforcement actions targeting illegal racing or commercial vehicle violations in this district?

themes_detail.label: Street Light Failures
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints reached 14 two weeks ago—a 261% increase from the 3.9-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.74)—raising safety and quality-of-life concerns if a section of the grid has gone dark, warranting investigation into infrastructure maintenance.
evidence: 14 street light complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.9 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Aligns with street condition spike, suggesting area-wide infrastructure issue
reporting_angles: Evening walkthrough: Identify dark blocks and interview residents about safety impact
Department of Environmental Protection source: Was there planned maintenance, outages, or equipment failures in specific neighborhoods 2–3 weeks ago?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Activity
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 3 two weeks ago (2300% above 0.1 weekly average, z-score: 8.69), a historically unusual surge that may signal either aggressive enforcement action, street-vending business disputes, or regulatory confusion—worthy of investigation into what caused the sudden complaints.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Aligns with community board budget requests for MWBE business support, suggesting existing vendor ecosystem tension
reporting_angles: Street vendor interviews: Talk to food cart and small-business vendors about recent enforcement encounters
DOC/SLA source: Was there a crackdown or policy change 2–3 weeks ago? Context around permit compliance or illegal vending?
